utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-14/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Two short administrative matters. First, as I think the Chamber knows, we would be grateful for a short ex parte hearing. I understand the practical difficulties about setting one up at the beginning of the session. Knowing a little about what's at stake, there may be some urgency or there may be some need to deal with it as swiftly as possible; possibly at the end of the morning session. If we were to have some time, might that be possible?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, the alternative is 9.15 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: My concern is more what may follow in relation to the work of other parts of the institution, but if the Chamber is aware of the subject matter in general terms, and is convinced that 9.15 tomorrow morning will be time enough to deal with it, then 9.15 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Nice, we have only the vaguest idea, because we have had a very general message. Is there any reason it has to be dealt with today as opposed to 9.15 tomorrow morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Providing other parts of the institution are able to respond in time, 9.15 tomorrow should be all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm afraid that is so elliptical I don't know what that refers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That's a problem, isn't it? I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I leave it to your judgement. If you urge us to have the hearing today, we will do it today, provided we get on with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I will review it at the break and let you know informally whether it's necessary. The second small administrative matter relates to Brigadier Duncan, who is coming back this week. He provided his diary, and the Chamber will remember the concerns I expressed at the end of the time when he gave his evidence. But he has provided the extracts from his diary entirely voluntarily, blanked out, and so that's not a problem, and I think they've been served already. If not, they -- I think they have been. But before Mr. Sayers deals with that, in the letter by which they've been provided, he also asks that he may be provided with some milinfosums for particular dates. Well, now, I haven't checked whether they have already been exhibited so that they are in a sense public documents, and there's probably no reason why he shouldn't have them; they are documents of record to which he would have made a contribution. But as he is partway through giving his evidence, I checked that nobody will object to his having access, and if so, we will provide him copies of milinfosums for the 9th, 12th, 13th, and 19th of May, the 11th of June, 27th of September, and 6th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: As Mr. Nice says, Mr. President, we have received some small extracts from Brigadier Duncan's diary. The one concern that I have with respect to the blacking-out of entries is that there are entries that concern events about which the brigadier testified, and you have, for example, a sentence about the event, a sentence about the event one sentence later, and then an intervening sentence just blacked out, and we don't have any way of verifying that the item that was blacked out is of a purely personal nature. Of course, if the Prosecution represents that it is, then we will take the Prosecution at its word; but it seems odd to have a sentence, that appears to be part of a discrete discussion of an event, blacked out without really any explanation for that given to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, it was really as a concession to you that that order was made. It's been done voluntarily by the witness, and the fact is that this is his private diary. Now, our ruling before has been that these diaries have to be protected because of the privacy of the individual, and he was given by the Court the power to determine what should be disclosed and what not. And in my view -- I haven't discussed it, of course, but in my view, you've got what you're entitled to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: We're obviously in the Trial Chamber's hands in that regard, and it turns out that the parts of the -- actually there are two sets of documents, extracts of which we were given, and they are both extremely helpful, and we are very grateful for the Court's indulgence in that regard, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: With respect to the request to consult the milinfosums, my reaction is that I don't see why not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: They form part of the pertinent materials in this case, and I think the brigadier is perfectly entitled to take a look at them if he wishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, if he had asked in the middle of the trial, while giving his evidence, if he could look at a milinfosum to refresh his memory, then presumably it would have been allowed, so I can see no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: We are completely in agreement, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'll act accordingly, and I'll raise the general concerns of the Ministry of Defence about diaries later, when the witness comes back, so as not to interrupt the flow of today's evidence. I gather there is an objection being taken in relation to today's witness, and I'll let Mr. Scott deal with that in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the record, we are sharing the view of the Kordic Defence in the raised matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is about the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Right -- no, I'm sorry, there's a misunderstanding. Related to the issue of the Duncan diary and milinfosums.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, if I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: -- if that is an appropriate moment -- and let me continue in the Croatian language, because it may be a little bit more difficult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is it a matter that you want to raise about the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We better go into private session then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, is it correct that in approximately the latter part of 1992, the first part of 1993, some several hundred people lived in what might be called the Santici area in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also correct that approximately 70 per cent of that population just referred to, in your estimate, was Croat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it also correct that in that village area, there were something like 15 Muslim or Bosniak houses in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, for purposes of the Court, if the witness has in front of him -- I believe you do there, Witness U -- a map which is marked as Z2271, although the usher might need to -- I'm sorry, some assistance. And I think, for these purposes, there is no reason why this can't be on the ELMO. It would be, I think, the easiest way for everyone. If you can focus on -- all right. That's okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you start with -- orient yourself to Vitez, can you point out on the map where Santici is located, and then perhaps the camera can zoom in on that particular portion, if you can find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, the video is not terribly clear. I'm not sure if -- okay. That's fine. All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're pointing now to the village of Santici, which, on the map, is probably something like oh, three or four centimetres to the right of Vitez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just, by way of further orientation, point out the village of Ahmici, which I believe you will find a little further to the right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's, in fact, rather misleading, isn't it? Because Ahmici is right next door to Santici.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. In fact, that was my next question of the witness. If you look at this map, it looks like there is considerable distance; but I think the witness will indicate that it is, to use the Court's word, somewhat misleading.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, how close, in fact, on the ground, is Santici to Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that locality seems to be joined. It's about 500 metres from my home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say, Witness U, that the two villages in a sense kind of meld together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they do meld together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct that perhaps -- you just indicated that what might be considered, if we can use the term in villages this small, the centre of Ahmici would be about 500 metres from your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move forward: Is it correct, sir, that on the 18th of October, 1992, the HVO attacked Santici. At about 8.00 that morning you heard gunshots and went to the southwest balcony of your house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw HVO soldiers running between the houses. You recognised some of the soldiers as your neighbours, although you did not know their names, or at least all of their names. They wore camouflage uniforms and camouflage bulletproof vests and were carrying weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one of the HVO soldiers appeared to you, to your observation, to be going in the direction of the HVO headquarters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say "HVO headquarters" in this particular context, are you referring to a local headquarters, if you will, in Santici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you can look at Exhibit Z1982, the aerial photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I'll have to clarify here: This reference to a building 15 is keyed to a different diagram. It should have been simply taken out of the outline, I suppose, but it was a key to an earlier statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at Exhibit 1982, is it correct, sir, that the HVO headquarters that you're referring to now was in building or location 4?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to being a headquarters or a gathering -- a meeting place, that was also the house of someone named Colic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving forward, on the 18th of October, as you began a few minutes ago, you saw a man named Nenad Santic running down the road from his house wearing a camouflage uniform and carrying an automatic rifle. He turned the corner at the Pican Cafe and headed north on the road to -- in the direction of Pirici, in the direction of this same HVO headquarters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you can just remind me, I apologise, for the correct pronunciation of that cafe: Pican?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pican. Pican.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the Exhibit 1982, is that the location number 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you know that Nenad Santic was a Croat and the commander of the -- the very local commander of the HVO in the Santici area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About 30 minutes after seeing what you described in the last couple of minutes, you saw a yellow flat-bed truck with a three-barrel anti-aircraft gun mounted on the back; this same Mr. Santic was on the back of the truck with the anti-aircraft gun; you saw the truck was going in the direction toward Ahmici; and after this, you heard heavy firing. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This same truck then came back and stopped in front of your house. Mr. Santic aimed the anti-aircraft gun at your house. About this time, Ivo Vidovic and Anto Vidosevic came out of the Pican Cafe and told Mr. Santic not to shoot at your house and, in fact, he did not; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this same truck with the anti-aircraft gun was then parked in front of Ivo Vidovic's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During these events around the 18th of October of 1992, a 19-year-old Muslim man was killed. You also saw Sakib Pezer trying to stop his house from burning. Anes Pezer told you several days later that his house and the mosque had also been struck by bullets; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Shortly after the 18th of October, sir, is it correct that again this same Nenad Santic, then also a Miro Josipovic and another man named Zeljko, came to your house; they searched the house and found the pistol for which your father, in fact, had a permit; and they took the pistol and your father to the local HVO headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn from your father, sir, that at that time, Mr. Santic threatened or made actions toward, in fact, beating your father at the HVO headquarters, but in the end, he did not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. True.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, Witness U, I'm going forward a few days, to the 23rd of October. On that day, were you sleeping in your room when you again heard shooting, when a red van -- you got up, looked out. There was a red van in front of your house with the black letters "HVO" painted on the front of the van?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What else did you see at that time? What was happening outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw a soldier holding a rifle aiming at the sky, but he was saying, "Balijas, balijas," and firing shots in the air, and others were breaking the glass (redacted). They looted the store, and after that, they boarded the van and headed towards Vitez. Then they paused, and when they stopped, one could hear two explosions. After that, they went on towards Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to determine, then, you and your family, soon after this event, that, in fact, two hand grenades had been tossed into the (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Two grenades were tossed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that about five minutes after this, again the same Mr. Nenad Santic and Zeljko Livancic arrived; your father told them what had happened, told them that the van had gone in the direction of Vitez; Mr. Santic was heard telling Livancic that they should go toward Vitez. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also correct that about 30 minutes later, Mr. Santic and Livancic came back to the house with three HVO soldiers, one of whom you recognised or was called, again, Ivo Vidovic, and another was -- perhaps you can remind me about his name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Anto Papic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All five of these men, including Mr. Santic, were wearing camouflage uniforms with HVO patches; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two of them had automatic rifles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this same Zeljko Livancic had previously attacked and beaten your father in a Croat store in Santici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, concerning these hand grenades being thrown (redacted), can you tell us, Witness U, to your knowledge was anyone ever arrested or punished in connection with that incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, nobody ever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court whether you believed that Mr. Santic, in fact, would do something about it, about this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said he was going towards Vitez to see what it was about, and when he came back he said that HVO soldiers were sleeping at the roadblock and they had not seen any man. Before that, he searched the house and was attacking my father in the HVO headquarters, and then he seized the weapon for which we had a permit, on no grounds at all. He gave us a piece of paper, "Nenad Santic, Commander of the Santici HVO."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All these events leading you to the conclusion that you did not expect Mr. Santic to take, in fact, any action about this incident (redacted) (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were not expecting him to do anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This incident, sir, caused, I take it, obviously some fear and stress to your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it did, very much so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, then that continuing on from about the time of these incidents in October 1992 and moving forward to April of 1993, that you and your family were regularly receiving threatening telephone calls because you were Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It appeared to you that during this time, after October 1992, conditions, relationships were deteriorating and it seemed to you that the Croats did not want the Muslims to live in Santici any more?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Sir, we're jumping to the 15th of April, 1993. Can you tell the Court, do you recall anything unusual about that day? Obviously, I think, at this point you know it was the day before some other tragedy, but on the 15th of April, was there anything unusual to you about that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I was at school and everything was as usual. I came home, got ready all my things for school the next day, and I didn't to school then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, Witness U. The last question pending was: On the 15th of April, do you recall anything unusual about that day, anything you saw around the Santici, Ahmici area that seemed unusual to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, nothing happened. As I said, I was at school in Vitez. I came back and everything was as usual. So I put together my things that I needed for the next day and that was that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were going to school in Vitez at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court, is it correct that on the 15th of April, or the preceding days, for that matter, was there any ABiH or Muslim military activity in Santici, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct that you did not see in that area any defensive earthworks or positions, military positions, either existing or being prepared there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, directing you then to the next day, the 16th of April, can you tell us what happened starting early that morning, and perhaps you can tell us part of this story in your own words.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the morning we heard a powerful explosion. My brother and I were in our room, and we went to our parents' room. My brother said to our father that there was this explosion, and our father said that he knew that. We all got up and came out into the hallway because it was shielded and that is where we were. Then we heard gunfire shots which came from the direction of Pican's cafe and Anto Vidosevic's house into my room and my brother's room and my father's room. Then we went down to the ground floor, and we took along our pillows and quilts with us because we decided that we should be there and not go anywhere. After that, we heard somebody say, "Boss, Boss, come out of the house." My father opened the door and said, "I have no weapons. I surrender." The soldier then ordered us to come out with our hands up and we did that. He took us across the street to a fence and told us to look in the opposite direction and turn our backs on our house. We could hear them breaking the windows and entering the house. One of them then asked, "Do you have any weapons?" Father said, "We don't." He said, "If we find any, we'll slit the throats of all of you."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did these men, the ones who were outside your door, how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were in camouflage uniforms and they were also painted with some creams on the face, and they had HVO flashes. One of them then told my father to come into the house, and my father stayed there for a while and then came back. He told us then that they had taken the money which we had and his wallet. Then I heard them talk and say, "What are we to do with them?" One of them said, "Well, take them to where the others are." So he told us to move down the main road, and we went for about (redacted) metres and then turned into the yard of Mustafa Dedic, Mujo. We reached his house, which was on fire, and there I saw Munib Ribo and Mustafa lying down killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we go too far ahead, a few details. When the HVO soldiers approached your house, I take it your family dog became concerned, was barking and an HVO soldier shot and killed your dog; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The money that was taken from your father or from inside the house, this was approximately 29.000 Deutschemarks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, 29.000 in the green safe, and I don't know how much he had in his wallet. As we were passing along the road, I saw that there were many soldiers in front of Pican's cafe and they were laughing at us. They were also wearing camouflage uniforms and their faces were painted in different colours. Then I saw the bodies of Ribo Munib and Mustafa Dedic. Then one of the two told my brother to open the door of the garage, of Mustafa Dedic's garage, and they told me and my mother to go into the garage. My brother also tried to enter the garage, but he told him to go back and to lock the garage. After, that I heard shots immediately. I peeped through the openings on the garage doors, the openings between the boards, and I saw my father and brother lying there dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did they kill your father and brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did they? Why were they killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because they were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had your father or brother offered any resistance at any time during that morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no resistance at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In fact, I'm momentarily referring back to paragraph 32, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the HVO tried to enter the garage at your house, your brother, in fact, offered to open the door for them rather than have the door broken; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes, he offered the keys of the garage and of the car but the soldier said nothing. He continued breaking down the door and that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before you got to the garage where your father and brother were killed, you said at the house of Mujo Dedic you saw the bodies of two other Muslim men, Mujo Dedic and Ribo Munib; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we can look at Exhibit Z1982, the aerial photograph. Was Mr. Dedic's house -- is that location number 5?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was burning at the time when you walked by the house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was burning. We were standing next to it and it was burning. It was very hot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you look now, in fact, at the photograph, you can see that the roof is burned off of the house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the location of the garage where your father and brother were killed, was that at location number 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Continue on, please. What happen then after your father and brother were killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that we were told we mustn't go out, not even to the toilet or to drink water, and if anyone went out, he would be killed. After that, I recognised Semren. His nickname was Zuti. I recognised him. He was masked, but he was easily recognisable, and he responded to a woman calling him by name,"Semren, Semren, Zuti." I also saw Drazenko Vidovic there. We were there for a while and then we were transferred to Nesib Ahmic's house, which was partly burned down, and we spent the night there. In the morning --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, before you go on, this Semren, was his first name -- apart from his nickname "Zuti," was his name Ivica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes, his name is Ivica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you went to Nesib Ahmic's house, which was partly burnt but partly still extant, and you spent the night there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Then in the morning some Croats in civilian clothes came and took us to the HVO headquarters. We were there. I sat with Heleg Munib, right next to Heleg Munib, and he told me if anything were to happen to him that I should let his son know that it was Nenad Santic who was to blame for everything. He had planned everything and that everything started from him. After that, two members of the HVO came in. Again they were wearing camouflage uniforms, and they took Hasim and his two sons. They wanted to take Haris Dedic as well, but his mother begged, "Don't. Don't take him. You've killed his brother and father already so leave him." So didn't take him. They took Hasim and his two sons and Munib Heleg. After some time, Nikica Plavsic walked into the room, nicknamed Slikar. Hasim's wife asked Nikica where her husband and two sons were, and he said that special forces had killed them and not to expect them to return, and that they were going to go to Pirici to set fire to everything and kill everyone as they had done in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me stop you there for a moment, Witness U. As you were still being held in the garage, is it correct that there was another young man, you just referred to him, Haris Dedic, and that his father and brother, who were both Muslims, had also been killed earlier that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, his father and brother had been killed, and they wanted to take him and kill him too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is when his mother intervened and said, "You have already killed my husband and other son, so don't take him"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the record is clear on these four men, the four men who were taken out, one was this man Heleg, and then Hasim Ahmic and his two sons, Zenur Ahmic and Amir Ahmic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court, sir, did you, in fact, ever see those four Muslim men alive again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Never. I never saw them again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can ask the usher to show you Exhibit Z1540.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the man that you saw that day, and talked to, and then was taken away, named Heleg?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, is it correct that it was your conclusion or belief that the HVO soldiers who were in Santici on the 16th of April were helped, or, in fact, maybe included some of your neighbours, who were HVO, in doing these things that you've described in the last few minutes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court why, in your view, was it necessary that some of the Croats and your neighbours from Santici were, in fact, involved in these events, that is, in carrying them out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because people from the outside, if you bring people from the outside, they can't distinguish between Muslim and Croat houses. That is why I believe, and that is true, that our neighbours helped them, that our neighbours were involved in this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the Court's general assistance, Witness U, have you heard it to be something of a -- I'll use the worth "myth," or incorrect information, that some people say that all Muslim houses have four-sided roofs and that all Croat houses have two-sided roofs, and that's the way that anyone looking at the house can tell whether it's a Croat house or a Muslim house? Is that true or false?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You cannot tell which house is whose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can direct your attention and the Court's attention again to Exhibit 1982, if I can direct your attention to locations 2 and 15, can you tell us whether, to your knowledge, Croats lived in those buildings, or Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Croats lived there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yet when you look at the photograph, you can see that, from the still-existing roofs, these were four-sided roofs; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, in Santici, sir, did you see any Croat houses, houses where Croats lived, burned or damaged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Neither burnt nor damaged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereas if you look -- and if the Court can take the time at its own leisure to look at Exhibit 1982, its more length, you can look at, for instance, locations 11, 10, 12, 7, 8, and a number of others -- is it correct, Witness U, you can see that all the roofs on those houses have been burned off?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move forward, then. After you had spent some time in the garage from which these four men were taken, what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that, two UNPROFOR vehicles arrived, and the women with babies wanted to go to Zenica. Then Jevco came running from Pirici, and he took those UNPROFOR vehicles away from us. Later on we saw them stop for a moment and then turn around and go off in the direction of Vitez. After that, all of us together headed towards Vitez. We were stopped there at a point called Dubravica, the old railway station. We stopped there, and then, again, a Croat came by. His kum was Islam Ahmic, and he had been killed, and he had put his women and children in his car, and so he picked up me and another boy, Ahmic Elmir, and took us to Vitez. My mother stayed behind. She told me to go. She couldn't come. After that, we reached Vitez. I asked him to go back, if he could, to get my mother. He said he would try, but he didn't manage. I don't know what happened. He didn't bring my mother over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, let me again stop on a few details. You used just now the word "kum"; with the interpreters' help, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When a baby is born, then somebody comes as a godfather, and that is a kum. So they had that kind of relationship, as families.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, before we move on, the HVO soldiers that you saw in Santici on the 16th of April, 1993, at least the ones that you recognised, is it correct, sir, that they were all from Santici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is Santici part of the Vitez municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it your understanding, therefore, at this time, that these HVO soldiers in Santici were part of the HVO Vitez Brigade and under the command and control of the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure the witness is in a position to so describe these events unless a proper foundation is laid.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me see if I can assist, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your living in the area and interacting with your Croat neighbours and seeing, in fact, some of these same men who you recognised on the 16th of April, did you know that there were in fact HVO members or soldiers in the Santici area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did know them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any information, in talking with any of these soldiers, what unit or brigade they were part of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I talked to Bruno Santic, and he lived in a place that is separated from Santici by the river. This place is called Donja Rovna. He told me that they belonged to the Busovaca Brigade, to Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we're jumping ahead in the outline now and perhaps confusing two different groups, so I will move forward. I think, as the Court indicated, we probably can't go further with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, as you then moved off from this garage and went toward Vitez and then ultimately to -- your mother stopped at the Dubravica school and did not go on to this apartment in Vitez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember, during these events, the HVO soldier's name who told you that you would be exchanged, the group of you would be exchanged and taken to -- again, to Vitez or Dubravica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Anto Papic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then you mentioned this Croat man who had picked up some of you and taken you to an apartment in Vitez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you at this apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For 17 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time when you were staying in Vitez, did you see any bodies, or burned houses, in Vitez in the area of where you were staying at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Referring back to the people who had stayed at the Dubravica school, did you ever talk afterwards to Haris Dedic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I spoke to him, and he told me that they had taken people to dig trenches, the prisoners. They took the prisoners to dig trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these prisoners, to your knowledge, were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Only Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move forward, then, again. Did there come a time when you left this apartment in Vitez and went to another location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we went to the elementary school in Vitez, and they said that the Red Cross was there, that we could apply and be registered, and we would be taken to Zenica. However, nothing came of that. We were there for three days. HVO soldiers were there. After that, this Croat came who had brought us to this apartment, and he took us to the road towards Zenica. It's a roundabout road through the mountains, and he told us to go alone, that he could not help us, saying, "Surely they will not shoot." So we headed off. We passed by the Muslim cemetery. HVO soldiers were there digging trenches, and I saw them drinking water. They didn't say anything to us. We went on, and then we heard shooting. Bullets flew over our heads, so we lay down. Later on, we came to the conclusion that those were snipers that were trying to hit us. And then we proceeded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you went on to Zenica, and is it fair to say, sir, that you then lived in Zenica for the rest of the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I lived in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Again, a couple of details. Just, in fairness, going back to the time you spent at the elementary school in Vitez, you did not see, during that particular occasion, any Muslims hurt or killed, and did not see any women or girls taken away at that location by the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the size of this group that you were on the road to Zenica with, how many people were you travelling with at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Eight to ten people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In concluding this part of these subjects, let me ask you to look at -- and let me be specific that these not be put on the ELMO, Your Honour, because they would be identifying, or at least some of them would be identifying. But if you can look, please, first, at Exhibit Z1986.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: These are going to be several -- four or five photographs, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The family shown in Exhibit 1986, who is that, or who is the man? Let's start with that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the late Ribo Munib. I saw him killed (redacted).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was one of the two men who you saw -- whose bodies you saw on the ground near Mujo Dedic's house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exhibit 1987 is just a different photograph of the same man and his family; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention, next, to Exhibit 1984. The man to the right of the photograph, with no shirt, is that your father?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is my father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the young man approximately in the middle of the photograph, with someone behind him in a striped shirt, is that your brother, who was killed on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that is my brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you in that picture, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, next to -- next to my brother, with a cap on the head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're the young boy in the white shirt; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who is to your brother's right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is my mother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exhibit 1985: Is that a photograph of your brother, who was killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving forward, then, Witness U -- are you okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew that this Nenad Santic was the HVO commander in Santici, and he was -- in your view, was he the one in Santici who was working the most or taking the most actions against the Muslims in Santici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It was Nenad Santic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During these events, or during 1992 and 1993, did you know of a man named Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I did know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did you know or understand Mr. Kordic to be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a highly influential person in Central Bosnia, and I believe that he -- I don't know how to put it -- that he was the leader down there of the HVO in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mr. Kordic in Santici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Directing your attention, then, to approximately the end of October period of 1992, was it around that time that you saw Mr. Kordic in Santici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, then, in your own words, what you saw of Mr. Kordic that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was coming back home from school, and across the road from my house was Nenad Santic, in a suit, and he was carrying a briefcase. I passed by him. I greeted him and went home. After that, I saw a jeep coming up, and I saw that there was the driver inside and Dario Kordic. Nenad Santic got into the jeep, and they drove off in the direction of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any particular reason that you said hello to this Mr. Santic as you walked by on your way home from school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He told Elmir Ahmic to tell all of us that we would have to greet him whenever we saw him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "all of us," sir, who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Us Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Scott. I should like to ask the witness whether Mr. Santic had an official position in Santici at that time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was an HVO commander in Santici. I don't know exactly whether he had any formal position, but I know that he was the HVO commander in Santici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, if you come to a convenient moment, we'll adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: There are one or two further questions on this topic, Your Honour, but we can take it just as easily after a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll adjourn now until half past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, before moving on then, if you could look again at --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before moving on, can you look again at Exhibit 1982, the aerial photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point out approximately on the photograph where you saw Mr. Santic standing or waiting when you then later saw him being picked up in a car with Mr. Kordic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him opposite me. He was there between my house and Pican's restaurant. He was standing there on the corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Given that reference, I'm not going to ask that it be put on the ELMO for identification, because it may be identifying. Is it fair to say then -- let us go this way: The point where Mr. Santic was standing was something -- 50 metres or less from where you observed this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Less. About 30 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that there were two people in the car, a driver and then you saw Dario Kordic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, continuing on, can you tell the Court whether soon after when you saw this event in Santici, did you see Mr. Kordic on television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court what you saw and what you remember about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw that Dario Kordic and Slavica Josipovic, they were on television together. It was a meeting at Grude.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was this Slavica Josipovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She was Nenad Santic's sister.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did she work in the HVO headquarters in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court the approximate connection in time or relationship in time between seeing Mr. Santic and Mr. Kordic in Santici and then when you saw Mr. Kordic on television concerning the meeting in Grude?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was either that same evening or the next evening that I saw him on television.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on then, Witness U. Were you childhood friends with someone named Bruno Santic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this Mr. Santic, Bruno, had a brother by the name of Leonard Santic, nicknamed Leno?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these were the sons of Zvonko Santic and they lived in Donja Rovna in the municipality Busovaca; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you mentioned this earlier. Is it correct that Donja Rovna is close to Santici but on the opposite side of the Lasva River?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, is it correct to say, sir, that at least up until some point in time you and this Bruno Santic continued to be friendly toward one another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall an occasion when Bruno Santic said something to you about a military unit that he was a member of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He told me he was a member of a special unit which was Kordic's special unit. That's what it was called. He told me that the training was very hard and that many could not pass it and that -- something about Kordic having elected them -- selected specially for that unit and that some of them were his bodyguards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you understand where this unit was based or where this training was taking place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All I know is that it was in Busovaca, that the training ground was in Busovaca, but I really don't know where the training itself was taking place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you to look -- well, did you see any patches on, when you had this conversation, Bruno Santic? Did you see any insignia or patches on his uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He had an HVO patch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he have a brother -- did you see his brother on this particular occasion or at some point around this time see the two of them together; Leonard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw them both together and separately. We used to meet, and his brother had an HVO patch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me just ask you: Did one of them have an HV patch and the other have an HVO patch, or did they both have the came patches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One, Bruno, had an HV [realtime transcript read in error HVO] patch, and Leno had an HVO [realtime transcript read in error HV] patch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to look, please, at Exhibit 1458,1, and again because of some markings on that exhibit, I ask that it not be displayed and that it will be sealed, but if the witness and the Court can look at a hard copy, if you will, of 1458,1. Sir, is that a drawing that you made of the patch, the HV patch or insignia that you saw on Bruno Santic's uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I thought the witness said that Bruno had the HV patch and Leonard had the -- Bruno had the HVO patch and Leonard had the HV patch. Perhaps you could clear that up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm looking back at the transcript myself, but let's just simply ask again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between the two brothers, sir -- can you just be as clear as possible in response to the Judge's question -- which of the brothers had the HV patch and which had the HVO patch?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bruno Santic, Bruno Santic had an HV patch and Leonard Santic's patch was HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was Bruno Santic who told you that he was in this Dario Kordic special unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Bruno Santic say anything to you about how the members of this unit were selected? I'm sorry, I'm looking at the transcript. I don't know if you answered that or not. Did he tell you how the members of this unit were selected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That he -- that Dario Kordic selected them himself and that the training was very hard and that it lasted for two months. That's what he told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Is it fair to say, Witness U, that you can recall seeing Mr. Kordic on television approximately five times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These were usually something we might call press conferences?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would Mr. Kordic be dressed during these televised press conferences?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At times he would be in a camouflage uniform and at times he was in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct that you remember seeing Colonel Blaskic at least two of these same press conferences together with Mr. Kordic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear Mr. Kordic speaking on the radio?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what, if anything, do you remember him saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that occasion, he talked about war. I didn't really understand what he was saying, but he said something like the Muslims and Croats could not go on living together any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, one last other point of information, sir: During the time of the war, had you also known or heard of an HVO unit which wore black uniforms and were called the Jokeri?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear about them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness U.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honours, may we be the first ones to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Kovacic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm Bozidar Kovacic. I'm a lawyer from Rijeka, from Croatia. I'm sorry we have to look at one another across this. I am the counsel for the second accused, Mario Cerkez, in this case, together with my colleague Mr. Mikulicic. I am sorry, I know you suffered losses in this war, but I nevertheless need to ask you some questions so as to clarify certain points. We both speak the same language, so I should -- and this same holds true of me; let us try to make pauses so that the interpreters have time to translate both answers and questions. I trust I shall be rather brief. So, Witness U, could you tell me, at that time, you were a young man in the secondary school, at the time when all those things happened. In 1992, before the incident you told us about in October '92 took place, did you see any village guards before that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I used to see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So tell us, were those village guards of a mixed composition? That is, did both Muslims and Croats from the village take part in them? Or were they monoethnic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the beginning, they were mixed, and later on Croats took those village guards upon themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did those men who participated in village guards wear some uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Croats did. The Muslims did not have any uniforms, so they were in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it a rule without an exception, or was it the general picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, some may have had a shirt or something, I mean a camouflage shirt or something, but very few of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that hold true of both parties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, no, this holds true only of the Muslim party. The Croats had uniforms with HVO flashes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did all the Croats wear the same kind of clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from what you know, what kind of weapons did the Croats serving on village guards have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Different types of weapons, but by and large, automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you know anything about how they obtained those weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Nenad Santic, whom you mentioned a couple of times, was he also part of these village guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not go out on guard duty, because he was an HVO commander in Santici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, the HVO in Santici, the only thing they did was go on guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Why, yes, and he was a commander. A commander won't go out to stand guard, would he?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you think that he was the one who issued the orders of assignment, and duties, and things like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you learn that? Was that common knowledge in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Nobody talked about that to you personally, showed you a paper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when he searched the house and seized our pistol, he gave us a piece of paper, and I have it at home in Bosnia. It said that a pistol of such-and-such make was being seized, and under it, it said, "HVO Commander, Nenad Santic."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The conflict that you told us about, or better said, the attack in October '92, that was, I believe, on the 18th of October. Are you quite sure that it was the 18th of October, or the 20th of October?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 18th of October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because, at that time, there was another skirmish because a roadblock was put up above the Catholic cemetery. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that down there -- that is, that a young man was killed in the village that night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him die?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear about the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All I heard was that he was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did not hear that it happened at that roadblock?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you do not know if he was killed at that roadblock?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me just one thing: This photograph which we used here, Z1982, I suppose you don't know when it was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It must have been taken after the conflict, after the HVO attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you do not know how long after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness wouldn't know, but no doubt the Prosecution, if it's important, can assist as to when this aerial photograph was taken. Mr. Scott, no doubt you can help us at some stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I can inquire, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, your house, as you come -- because on this photograph we do not see how this is turned, but the house that you indicated to us, which is marked number 1, as you come from Vitez, as you go to Busovaca, eastward, where is it? On the left-hand side of the road?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I apologise. It was really my fault. Okay, I'll go around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If at any time you want to go into private session, just ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think it will be necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So between those (redacted) in the place, were they competing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean, "competing"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, there are two (redacted) in a very small area. Were they rivals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the owner of (redacted) a Croat, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, you told us that some soldiers in a van came to your house, and then you found out that they'd thrown grenades (redacted) (redacted). Did you or your father or any other member of your family report that incident to the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wouldn't know exactly. I know that father called somebody by telephone, but I don't know what he said. He called Nenad and somebody else, but I don't know what about exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he asking Nenad Santic to intercede or something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. When he seized the weapon, he said if anything, then that we should call him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And the building number 4, which you marked and which you said housed the HVO headquarters in the village, was it its only purpose, or did it serve some other purpose, too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the ground floor was the headquarters, and they lived on the upper floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So wouldn't it be true to say that it was a private house, a private home, and that Santic used the ground floor as his commanding post?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All I know is that it was the HVO headquarters, and above it were residential premises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the ground-floor premises, were they used also for some village meetings when those were held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was HVO soldiers who usually gathered there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But wasn't it a place where people used to meet and hold meetings even before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that when those soldiers arrived one of them called your father to come out, calling him, "Chief, chief."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps recognise the voice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know who it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Anto Papic, who told you that you would be exchanged and so on. In an earlier statement you had said that he explicitly told you that he would take care of you and that nobody would kill you. Do you remember that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can I take it from this that Anto Papic wanted to calm you down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what he wanted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he did say what I just said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He was the guard there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, when you spent those 17 days in that apartment in Vitez, Vitez Television came there one day, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they made a feature about it, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You made a statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't speak during that filming?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They just filmed us and nobody said anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a TV set in that apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you later see that feature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that it had been broadcast?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear it, but I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that somebody told you that they saw you on television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They filmed us. We didn't say anything. This was very brief. They came with a camera and they left. I assume it was shown on television. Why else would they have filmed us?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in any event, you didn't make any statements?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said a moment ago, towards the end of your testimony, that Slavica Josipovic used to work in the HVO headquarters in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "HVO headquarters in Vitez," what institution do you mean or, rather, which building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know, for instance, that in the Vitez Hotel that the Operative Zone of the HVO had its headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that in the cinema in the Workers' University there was another headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard about the cinema while I spent 17 days there. Sulejman was taken to the cinema for interrogation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know in which building Slavica worked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know perhaps the name of the institution in which she worked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, Witness U, your village, Santici, is actually very close to the municipal border. Do you know where the border is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I just know that Rovna is across the Lasva, and further on I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In connection with the TV crew that came to the apartment that we have just mentioned, do you remember that Sulejman Dajic made a statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was, because he was taken twice to the cinema, as I just said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the TV Vitez studio was housed in the cinema hall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never heard that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You said in your testimony that this Croat eventually took you to the road via Vjetrenica, the road that goes via Vjetrenica to Zenica. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from thereon you went on foot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that road, do you know what Sivrino Selo is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that it is some way removed from the road. I think so at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So once you start climbing along this road toward Vjetrenica, after a couple of kilometres you come to Sivrino Selo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, to the right. On the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that area was under the control of the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us that you walked all the way to Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did someone pick you up and drive you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stopped there and I was recognised by a friend, a family friend, and he put us in a car and he drove us there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where this was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You told us that you were detained in the elementary school in Vitez for three days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us which unit guarded that place? Who were the guards? Were they military police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: HVO soldiers in camouflage uniforms. I don't know whether they were the police or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You couldn't tell from any insignia what unit they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, did you ever see on television Mr. Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mr. Cerkez in Santici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the troops in Santici ever mention Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think I have no further questions for this witness, and thank you. Thank you, Witness U.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, before you finish, may I be sure that I have the position right, that there is no dispute or no challenge to the witness's evidence that soldiers in camouflage uniform with cream on their faces and HVO flashes came to his house on the 16th of April, and no challenge to the events of the day as he described them. Because if there is any challenge to that or any dispute, then it should be put so the witness has got a chance to deal with it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that you summarised our position well. We are not challenging the fact that certain HVO soldiers came to the house; secondly, we really do not know exactly what happened in Santici that morning. The only thing that we challenge is that they were not HVO soldiers of the Vitez Brigade. And the witness knows nothing about that. From the other questions and answers, it is evident that he did not recognise any closer insignia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, you were saying that you challenge what the witness said, and that is HVO troops intervened at Santici and that they were apart of the Vitez Brigade. Mr. Kovacic, I am addressing you. You said that you are challenging that the soldiers that intervened in Santici were part of the Vitez Brigade. Are you also contesting that Santici was territorially a part of the Vitez command?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. No, I'm not challenging that. Territorially and according to administrative municipal borders, Santici is a part of Vitez municipality, but we will show documents later on to show this, that they're actually bordering with the neighbouring municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Naumovski:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. U, allow me to introduce myself. I am attorney Mitko Naumovski, one of the Defence counsels for Dario Kordic. I have several questions for you but please remember the warning to wait a minute for your answer until the question has been translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, about these events in Ahmici and Santici, you have had occasion to hear extensive testimony, so I have only a few questions for this witness so as not to remind him of the terrible tragedy that he experienced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. U, you gave five statements to the investigators of The Hague Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you testified in the case against General Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from those statements, did you also make a statement for the centre of the security services in Zenica or some other body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you went to school you went to the elementary school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I went to the secondary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What year were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
