utterances.text: First year, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you keep any kind of school diary or something like that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My colleague has asked you something about this so I have just one more. If I understood you well, you have no knowledge at all about the fact that at the end of October 1992 there was an obstacle placed on the Vitez-Busovaca road and that there was a conflict there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not only do you not have any personal knowledge, but you didn't hear anything about it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the attack occurred, I heard that this young man had been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that is what you said occurred on the 18th of October?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The secondary school you went to, it was a school attended by members of all ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you went to school together until the 15th of April, 1993? That was the last day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you spoke about this event in October, if I understood you correctly, you just saw soldiers wearing camouflage uniforms, on the 18th of October?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I saw them with HVO insignia and that is what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you recognised your neighbours, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you don't know the names of those neighbours that you recognised that moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those I knew, I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the people you recognised is Nenad Santic, that you have spoken about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You already said that he was the local commander of the HVO, as you've said, in Santici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You heard that Nenad Santic was killed later in Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard something about it, but I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were a school pupil, and you probably don't know much about these things, but I still have to ask you: Do you have any personal knowledge about the organisation of Territorial Defence in Santici, Ahmici, and that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nor were any members of your household or your neighbours a member of the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, my brother was a member.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence in Santici, did it have a separate department? Was it separate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they, then, part of the Ahmici department?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where, then, where was your brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was part of the Vitez Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us now go on to the events of April '93. You told us that a Croat helped you and transferred you to that apartment where you spent 17 days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we tell his name, or will that contribute to disclosing your own identity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As he is known in Vitez, I would rather not mention his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Never mind, then. A few more questions about this. Towards the end of your testimony today, you said that you saw soldiers with Jokers insignia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did, and I heard about them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know who the commander of the Jokers was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know the names of any Jokers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us now go on to a few questions linked to Mr. Dario Kordic that you mentioned today. You said that you were a student of the first year of secondary school, so I assume you were not a member of any party; you were not involved in politics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also had no military duties, so you have no knowledge about military matters; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, as a student of the first year of secondary school, have any knowledge about the method and organisation of the authorities in Vitez municipality in those days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know who held which office, and that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today you spoke about your views regarding the position of Mr. Dario Kordic. That was a conclusion of your own, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said what I thought.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is, if that is the conclusion you came to, what was that conclusion based on? You did not follow political events, you didn't know who held which position, so what is your conclusion based on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dario Kordic had his special unit -- may I ask you a question? Why did he appear in public wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness U, I'm afraid you've got to answer the questions rather than ask them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just asked you to explain what your conclusion was based on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But I already have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because he was on television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and because he had a special unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you only know about it from what Bruno Santic told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Bruno Santic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which Santic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bruno Santic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, Bruno; I see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Bruno, Bruno.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I said Susnja; I'm sorry. Bruno Santic. That's right. Let us focus for a moment on this event when you said you saw Dario Kordic in Santici. You don't know exactly what date it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please: Today you said that you first saw Nenad Santic standing at the bus station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Right across the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't have to tell us, just for identification purposes, in your own interest. You said that the distance was some 30 metres from which you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were watching from the first floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the statement I received today from the Prosecutor, it says explicitly that you were watching from a distance of some 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 30 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're saying that today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I'm saying 30 metres, the distance was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just reminding you of what you told the investigator. Is that a mistake, then? At that interrogation, Mr. Patrick Lopez-Terres was present, one of the Prosecutors, and it says here that you were watching this from a distance of 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 30 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Nenad Santic was in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But otherwise, he always wore a uniform in October '92?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly he wore a uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what direction did this car come?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the direction of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us a little more about the car? The colour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember the colour. I know it was a jeep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A military or civilian vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A civilian vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you perhaps see the license plate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please: You said that you immediately recognised Mr. Kordic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was he sitting in the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was sitting on the side closest to my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in relation to the driver?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was sitting so that I could see him at the window.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what seat in the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Behind. Behind, to the right of the driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what his hairstyle was like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Kordic had a short haircut. His hair was cut short.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see whether he was wearing glasses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was wearing glasses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have a thick frame on those glasses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice what kind of clothing he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, but on television, I saw him in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't notice what clothing he had on. How long did the car stand there while Nenad Santic got in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just for a minute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe less than a minute, just for Nenad Santic to get on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it wasn't less than a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All these questions, are you contesting the fact that Kordic was in Santici, or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Mr. Kordic was not in Santici. That is our position. If I may proceed?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. U, your first statement was given a year and six months after all these events, on the 17th of October, 1994. I assume you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Up to a point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, describing this event, quite contrary to what you said today, that Dario Kordic was wearing a camouflage uniform with an HVO patch on his shoulder.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, what I said today is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, unfortunately I only have this single copy of that statement; but if necessary, if you think it is necessary, I should like to show the witness this statement so he can read himself what he said and what he signed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You can read out to him that he said that Mr. Kordic was in a camouflage uniform, and he says that that's wrong. Now, is there anything else that you want to put in the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I'll come to that immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Speaking about this event, you just said that you saw Mr. Dario Kordic and Nenad Santic, didn't you? But when you made this first statement, and that is the second reason why I wish to show it to you, you said that Mr. Kordic was with Nenad Santic and Slavica Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I must have been confused, because I saw Slavica Josipovic on television that night with Kordic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand what you said, but I have to tell you that in this statement, there is no mixup. You then said that Dario Kordic and Slavica entered his car.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can read out the whole sentence, if Your Honours permit. Shall I read the whole sentence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Unless it adds anything to what you've put to the witness -- you've put what the statement says; the witness says that he was confused. I don't know that we can take it, really, very much further than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honours, with respect, but I believe that from this context, you will also see whether this is a confusion of some sort or something else. That is why I thought it would be better if I read it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Read the statement, then. But before you do, have the Prosecution got the passage? You have?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have that one, and I think there is also --

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it is page 6 in the English version, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We do have it, and there is also a correcting later statement in which this statement was corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. If necessary, you can deal with that. You can read the sentence now, Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here it is: "Dario Kordic was with Nenad Santic and Slavica Josipovic. Slavica used to work for the HVO headquarters in Vitez. As I passed by, I greeted Nenad Santic, because we had to greet him. Dario Kordic was in a camouflage union [as interpreted] with an HVO flash. Slavica was in civilian clothes. Dario Kordic and Slavica entered his car and drove away." Now I've read the whole context.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just told you a moment ago that I was mixed up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you say here is not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What is true is that I saw Dario Kordic with Nenad Santic; that is, that Nenad Santic boarded his car and they drove away together. That is true, and I don't know what else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're denying what I've just read to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I'm not denying, but I was confused at the time and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There is no need to say anything more about this. You have put the matter. The witness has answered it. The matter is now plain. Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Speaking about Mrs. Slavica Josipovic, Slavica Josipovic was one of the prominent members of the HVO in Vitez. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Slavica Josipovic is, at present, a member of the presidency of the HVO -- of the HDZ in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I used to see her, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us move on to another topic, and that is on to Bruno, Leonard Santic, a couple of questions. If I understand the statement properly, I mean, the statement which was made in December 1998 in the presentation of Mr. Patrick Lopez-Terres, this Bruno Santic was a little bit older than you, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I think four years my senior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, not really a little bit, but if you say "four," then it's four?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us today -- let us not repeat all that -- what unit he belonged to and so on and so forth. Did he also mention to you that he was also a member of the Busovaca Brigade, because that was his position there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And apart from that flash which you say was an HV, was his uniform in any way different from his brother's uniform, Leonard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Uniforms are the same, it's only that the flashes were different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we shall agree that, as you say, Leonard was a member of the Busovaca Brigade, the HVO Brigade in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Bruno Susnja -- no. There I go once again. Bruno Santic, you were on friendly terms with him? You were friends for a long time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We were friends for a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you must know that he never was in the HV?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But was he absent from home for a long time so that you would know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we were not all that close to keep visiting one another all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us today that only he was with that unit and that his brother wasn't. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He told me that he was with Kordic's special unit and that his brother wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you made this statement a year and a half after the events that I spoke about earlier, on the same page in the English version you also said that the two of them told you the whole story about that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. His brother was with him when he told me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I wanted to tell you is that what you said explicitly then was that Leonard was also a member of that unit together with his brother.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, only Bruno was a member.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you agree that you said earlier what I've just read to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I have no answer to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's agreed with it. Yes, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About six years and six months have elapsed more or less since the events that you spoke about. In conclusion, referring to what you heard on the radio, you said that Mr. Kordic was saying something about the war but that you didn't really get his meaning, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I did understand what he said, that the Muslims and the Croats could not go on living together anymore. That is one thing I understood very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But could you please define it closer? When did you hear it said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what year was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when you heard that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wouldn't really know when but I was at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, I must say this: You gave five statements. You also testified in the Blaskic case, which makes it the sixth time. This is the first time today that you are mentioning that Mr. Kordic ever said something on the radio. You never mentioned that before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: True. I did not deem it all that important, but now it turns out that it is very important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I know, but I also must tell you that when you made your first statement, you were asked to speak about relevant things and you immediately told them all that you knew about Mr. Kordic. At that time, of course, your memory was much fresher than now, six years later.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, maybe not. Maybe now I'm beginning to get a clear picture of it all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, for your patience. I have no more questions. I should also like to thank the witness. Re-examined by Mr. Scott:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, when your further statement was taken on approximately the 15th of December of last year, 1998 -- and I'll have to ask, obviously, for this to be translated to you rather than show it to you, the copy I have is English -- do you remember giving a statement at that time and now I'm quoting: "During my first interview, I had mentioned that Slavica Josipovic, Nenad Santic's sister, was there. Today I no longer remember whether she was. However, I do remember very well that on that same evening or on the day after the meeting, I saw Kordic, Santic, and Slavica Josipovic together in a televised report covering a demonstration which had taken place in Grude."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also say, on the 15th of December last year, that: "During my preceding interview, it was mistakenly stated that Bruno's brother, Leonard, was also a member of the special unit. Leonard was only a member of the HVO forces in Busovaca. I have not had any further contact with Bruno and his family since I left Santici."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness U, that concludes your evidence and you are released. Thank you for coming to the International Tribunal to give evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just wait a moment and then you can go.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The next witness is going to be taken by Mr. Lopez-Terres. Here he is. Just before we part from the last witness, as the Chamber knows, witnesses -- Croat witnesses of the type referred to by the last witness are not generally available to us for obvious reasons. I mention that because, of course, at some stage the Chamber may, and I don't know what the court's provisional attitude is going to be, but it may be thinking of calling witnesses on its own account, and such witnesses may or may not be more amenable to the summons of the Trial Chamber than they are to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Speaking of myself, I wasn't, but no doubt it can be considered. There was the matter which you wanted to raise before we start on the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. I understand the Chamber would prefer to deal with it at 9.15 tomorrow morning. I can make it at 9.15 tomorrow morning, although I have to see someone at I think half past 9.00 and a hearing in the other Chamber at 10.00. If because of the hour and knowing that it takes five minutes to change from one mode to another the Chamber would rather take the ex parte matter now, I'm in the Chamber's hands. What I have to say is, I think, very short, it's just a question of having the arrangements made for the ex parte hearing to be properly recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Rather than start on the witness for quarter of an hour, since we're not sitting this afternoon, it may be more convenient to deal with the ex parte matter now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Before we do, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: May I address the Court this one sentence please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You put me some questions after my cross-examination of the witness. I would just like to point out to the Prosecution's brief, the title is "Prosecution's Overview of Witnesses," dated May 1999, where the summaries for each witness are provided. You remember that. On page 10, under number 129, there is specification to which item of the indictment this witness corresponds. There is no -- this is not related to the counts which are related to my client. So it is even -- the Prosecutor, at least in this paper, does not see the relation with that evidence to the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. That's a matter we can deal with in due course. Yes. Now, unless there's anything else, we'd invite -- it may be easier if we rise for five minutes. We'll rise for five minutes and the court can be rearranged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: at 12.46 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 24th day of November, 1999 at 9:30 a.m.
